narrative:
The model determined that you have a 27% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an overwhelming probability, it was high enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the size of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the level of savings you have. 

The large loan amount of 11,054 DM was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. This is substantially higher than the average of about 3,020 DM among applicants who were approved. Larger requests naturally carry more risk for the bank.

Your checking account status of having no account worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward good credit. Among approved applicants, 59% also had no checking account, so this is quite common.

However, having unknown or no savings pushed the prediction back toward bad credit risk. This is fairly typical (33% of approved applicants also show no savings), but in combination with the high loan amount it still increased your overall risk profile.

Because the requested amount had the greatest influence and pulled strongly toward denial, the bank decided not to approve the loan.

You should consider applying again with a significantly smaller loan amount, or take time to build up verifiable savings before reapplying. This would directly address the main reasons for the current rejection. (218 words)
